\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{சிக்கனம்} (cikkaṉam)}{சிக்கனம் (cikkaṉam)}]{\ta{சிக்கனம்} (cikkaṉam) — thrift; economy}

\label{lesson:TA-C548-cikkanam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to persist, then the Tamil for to fix a date.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{சிக்கனம்}}
\textbf{\ta{சிக்கனம்}} — \emph{cikkaṉam} — \textquotedblleft{}thrift; economy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{சிக்கனமாக} \ta{இருந்தால்} \ta{பணம்} \ta{மிஞ்சும்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{cikkaṉamāka iruntāl paṇam miñcum.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you are thrifty, money will be left over.
\end{quote}

With -\ta{ஆக}: \ta{சிக்கனமாகச்} \ta{செலவு} \ta{செய்}, to spend carefully.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \textbf{\ta{சிக்கனம்}} (\emph{cikkaṉam}) is not settled: no dictionary we can check gives its source.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cikkaṉam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cikkaṉam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cikkaṉamāka iruntāl paṇam miñcum.} — If you are thrifty, money will be left over.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to persist, then the Tamil for to fix a date, then say \emph{cikkaṉam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{சிக்கனம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Thrift; economy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{திவாலாகு} (tivālāku)}{திவாலாகு (tivālāku)}]{\ta{திவாலாகு} (tivālāku) — to go bankrupt}

\label{lesson:TA-C548-tivalaku}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to fix a date, then the Tamil for thrift.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{திவாலாகு}}
\textbf{\ta{திவாலாகு}} — \emph{tivālāku} — \textquotedblleft{}to go bankrupt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{கடன்} \ta{அதிகமானால்} \ta{நிறுவனம்} \ta{திவாலாகும்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kaṭaṉ atikamāṉāl niṟuvaṉam tivālākum.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the debts grow, the company will go bankrupt.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ta{திவாலானது}, \emph{tivālāṉatu}.

An \ta{ஆகு} verb: the firm is the subject, so the past is \ta{திவாலானது}. Bankruptcy is \ta{திவால்}.

\begin{cousinweb}
In \textbf{\ta{திவாலாகு}} (\emph{tivālāku}) the verb is the native \ta{ஆகு}, \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{}; the origin of \ta{திவால்} (\emph{tivāl}), \textquotedblleft{}bankruptcy\textquotedblright{}, is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tivālāku}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tivālāku}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṭaṉ atikamāṉāl niṟuvaṉam tivālākum.} — If the debts grow, the company will go bankrupt.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to fix a date, then the Tamil for thrift, then say \emph{tivālāku} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{திவாலாகு} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To go bankrupt\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{ஏய்} (ēy)}{ஏய் (ēy)}]{\ta{ஏய்} (ēy) — to swindle; to evade}

\label{lesson:TA-C548-ey}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for thrift, then the Tamil for to go bankrupt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{ஏய்}}
\textbf{\ta{ஏய்}} — \emph{ēy} — \textquotedblleft{}to swindle; to evade\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{அவன்} \ta{வரி} \ta{கட்டாமல்} \ta{அரசை} \ta{ஏய்த்தான்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avaṉ vari kaṭṭāmal aracai ēyttāṉ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He cheated the government by not paying tax.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{ஏய்த்தேன்}, \emph{ēyttēṉ}.

The one cheated takes -\ta{ஐ}. Tax evasion is \ta{வரி} \ta{ஏய்ப்பு}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{ஏய்}} (\emph{ēy}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 899 gives \ta{ஏய்} (\emph{ēy}), \textquotedblleft{}to be fit, to resemble\textquotedblright{}, and in its strong form \textquotedblleft{}to tell a seeming truth, to deceive\textquotedblright{}, with \ta{ஏய்ப்பு}, \textquotedblleft{}deceit\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ēy}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ēy}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avaṉ vari kaṭṭāmal aracai ēyttāṉ.} — He cheated the government by not paying tax.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for thrift, then the Tamil for to go bankrupt, then say \emph{ēy} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{ஏய்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To swindle; to evade\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{மோசடி} (mōcaṭi)}{மோசடி (mōcaṭi)}]{\ta{மோசடி} (mōcaṭi) — a fraud; a scam}

\label{lesson:TA-C548-mocati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to go bankrupt, then the Tamil for to swindle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{மோசடி}}
\textbf{\ta{மோசடி}} — \emph{mōcaṭi} — \textquotedblleft{}a fraud; a scam\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{பரிசு} \ta{விழுந்ததாக} \ta{வரும்} \ta{குறுஞ்செய்தி} \ta{ஒரு} \ta{மோசடி}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{paricu viḻuntatāka varum kuṟuñceyti oru mōcaṭi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A text message saying you have won a prize is a scam.
\end{quote}

With \ta{செய்} (\emph{cey}): \ta{மோசடி} \ta{செய்}, to commit fraud.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \textbf{\ta{மோசடி}} (\emph{mōcaṭi}) is not settled: no dictionary we can check gives its source.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mōcaṭi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paricu viḻuntatāka varum kuṟuñceyti oru mōcaṭi.} — A text message saying you have won a prize is a scam.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to go bankrupt, then the Tamil for to swindle, then say \emph{mōcaṭi} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{ஊடுருவு} (ūṭuruvu)}{ஊடுருவு (ūṭuruvu)}]{\ta{ஊடுருவு} (ūṭuruvu) — to break into; to infiltrate}

\label{lesson:TA-C548-uturuvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to swindle, then the Tamil for a fraud.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{ஊடுருவு}}
\textbf{\ta{ஊடுருவு}} — \emph{ūṭuruvu} — \textquotedblleft{}to break into; to infiltrate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{திருடர்கள்} \ta{வங்கியின்} \ta{கணினிக்குள்} \ta{ஊடுருவினார்கள்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tiruṭarkaḷ vaṅkiyiṉ kaṇiṉikkuḷ ūṭuruviṉārkaḷ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Thieves broke into the bank's computer.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{ஊடுருவினேன்}, \emph{ūṭuruviṉēṉ}.

Into what takes -\ta{க்குள்}, \textquotedblleft{}into\textquotedblright{}: \ta{கணினிக்குள்} \ta{ஊடுருவு}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{ஊடுருவு}} (\emph{ūṭuruvu}) is a native compound: \ta{ஊடு} (\emph{ūṭu}), \textquotedblleft{}through, the middle\textquotedblright{}, and \ta{உருவு} (\emph{uruvu}), \textquotedblleft{}to pierce through, to penetrate\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 663).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to swindle, then the Tamil for a fraud, then say \emph{ūṭuruvu} again
\end{itemize}
